newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-MATCH-WINNER AFRIDI CRITICISED FOR WORK ETHIC.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MATCH-WINNER AFRIDI CRITICISED FOR WORK ETHIC.

text.p: Pakistan all-rounder Shahid Afridi, who inspired his side's crushing win in the first match of the World Series final against West Indies, earned a rebuke from his coach for his troubles on Sunday.
Afridi scored a hard-hitting half century and claimed three wickets, including the vital scalp of Brian Lara, as Pakistan won by four wickets on Saturday.
But Pakistan coach Mushtaq Mohammad, while pleased with Afridi's development, questioned the leg-spinner's work ethic.
"If he really applies himself to the job, I'm sure he's got the ability to do well. He lacks application, maybe it's because he's young," Mushtaq said of the teenager.
West Indies captain Courtney Walsh said he was troubled by his side's batting collapse, the second time in successive matches Pakistan have routed the middle order.
After cruising to 99 for no wicket, West Indies lost seven wickets for 24 runs over the next 10 overs.
"It's not something you want to repeat itself because if we bat this way again in Melbourne, we are going to have a hard time winning the finals," Walsh said.
Pakistan will have opener Aamir Sohail available for the second match of the best-of-three final.
Mushtaq said he did not know whether Sohail, who was suspended for one match for dissent during a match against Australia last Thursday, would return to the side.
"We have got to sit down and work it out. Either we will play an extra seamer or an extra batsman," he said.
West Indies have injury worries over pace bowler Curtly Ambrose and batsmen Carl Hooper and Adrian Griffith.
